dek.text: The comptroller proposes treating cloud computing and AI as hosted services outside the data processing tax. His own fiscal note estimates what Texas would stop collecting.

introduction.text: [Comptroller Don Huffines announced proposed amendments on November 18th](c2) to [Rule 3.308](c4). [They appeared in the Texas Register issue of November 20th](c45). [The proposal defines hosted technology services to include cloud computing, artificial intelligence and quantum computing](c25). [It says those services are not data processing and are not taxable](c20).
It is a proposal. [The earliest the comptroller can adopt it is December 20th](c43), and nothing in the record shows it adopted.

sections.heading: What the tax was written for

paragraphs.text: [Huffines says the Legislature taxed data processing in 1987](c7). [Under the proposed definition, a data processing service is one where the provider processes data the customer supplied and returns it in the format the customer asked for](c22). [Storing or manipulating data would not by itself count](c23). [Neither would a customer using a provider's software, platform or computing to process its own data](c24).
[The comptroller says the agency's earlier reading of the tax was too expansive](c21). [He intends the amendments to apply only from the date their adoption takes effect](c44).

sections.heading: What the comptroller's own note estimates

paragraphs.text: [The fiscal note in the Register puts the loss to the state's General Revenue Fund at {{money:c26}} in fiscal year 2027](c26). The estimate rises in every year it counts. [It reaches {{money:c31}} in fiscal year 2032](c31).

[Losses to units of local government, including cities, counties and transit authorities, are estimated at {{money:c32}} in fiscal year 2027](c32). [They reach {{money:c37}} in fiscal year 2032](c37).

[The same note finds the amended rule will have an insignificant effect on the state's economy](c38). [It says one further effect on sales tax remittances can't be estimated](c39). Every figure here is the comptroller's estimate of a proposed rule, not a measured loss. [The Texas Tribune's account of the cost rests on the comptroller's own estimates](c10).

[Comments go to Robin Robinson, the Associate Deputy Comptroller for Tax, by mail or by email](c40). [The comptroller must receive them within {{number:c41}} days of the proposal's publication in the Register](c41). Counted from the issue date, that is December 20th.

[Comptroller-elect Sarah Eckhardt takes over the office on January 1st, according to the Tribune](c17). [She asked Huffines in a letter to stop pursuing rule changes begun since August 1st](c15), and [he replied that he would keep making rules until he leaves office](c18). The record holds no statement of what the new comptroller would do with this rule if it is adopted.
